conventions.convention: The finite-mode algebra is initially an algebraic unital complex star-algebra quotient, with {a_i,a_j}=0, {a_i†,a_j†}=0 and {a_i,a_j†}=δ_ij 1. The zero-mode algebra is C.
The Hilbert pairing is first-variable-linear. Creation c(f) is complex-linear in f, and {c(f)*,c(g)}=⟨g,f⟩1; annihilation is conjugate-linear.
The Clifford comparison uses Q(Σ z_r e_r)=Σ z_r² and e_r²=+1, with self-adjoint basis generators. Majoranas are γ_(2j−1)=a_j+a_j† and γ_(2j)=i(a_j†−a_j).
Occupation signs count occupied indices strictly below the toggled mode. Operator products act rightmost first; empty products are identities.
Countable modes are indexed by positive integers; coding indices use N₀. Each new mode is appended last in the finite-stage inclusions.
Abstract fermionic Fock space is the Hilbert completion of the algebraic orthogonal sum of exterior powers, with vacuum 1 in degree zero, under Countable Choice.
The arbitrary-Hilbert-space CAR completion assumes Countable Choice; the explicitly enumerated countable-mode completion and occupation branch do not.
A choice-free bounded CAR representation includes specified bounded adjoints on a nonzero Hilbert space; it does not assume adjoint existence for arbitrary bounded operators.

load_bearing.statement: For every integer n≥0, the algebraic finite-mode CAR star-algebra is star-isomorphic under the occupation representation to M_(2^n)(C). Every unital star-representation on a nonzero Hilbert space has the matrix-unit amplification form and is isometric. The universal C*-norm equals the matrix norm.

The signed occupation toggles satisfy the CAR and are mutual adjoints. For the displayed ordered products, E_(S,T)e_U=δ_(T,U)e_S. Consequently the occupation representation maps onto End(F_n)≅M_(2^n)(C), including n=0.
For n≥0 and Q(Σ z_r e_r)=Σ z_r² on C^(2n), the displayed Majorana assignments give inverse star-isomorphisms Cl⁺(C^(2n),Q)≅CAR_n^alg, with a_j mapping inversely to (e_(2j−1)+i e_(2j))/2.

If F⊆G are finite-dimensional complex inner-product subspaces of a Hilbert space H, the generator-preserving map CAR^alg(F)→CAR^alg(G) extends to an isometric unital star-homomorphism between their finite-dimensional C*-completions.

For every set I, the canonical complex space ℓ²(I,C) is complete, its finitely supported families are dense, and its coordinate vectors form an orthonormal basis. This result uses no choice principle.

Assume Countable Choice. On fermionic Fock space over a first-variable-linear complex Hilbert space H, wedge creation extends boundedly with norm ||f||. With A(f)=C(f)*, the same-type anticommutators vanish and {A(f),C(g)}=⟨g,f⟩I.

Every bounded countable CAR family with specified bounded adjoints on a nonzero complex Hilbert space induces a unique contractive unital star-homomorphism from CAR_N. The universal represented norm on the local union equals its inductive-limit norm, attained by the occupation-space representation.
The countable occupation representation is irreducible. The common annihilator kernel is the vacuum line, whereas the common creator kernel is {0}.

concerns.concern: The Statement calls the algebraic union “$\mathsf{CAR}_0$”, but the definition and displayed universal-norm formula call it CAR_loc; CAR_0 already denotes the zero-mode algebra C. This is a notation slip in the Statement.

The Statement describes a “unital $*$-homomorphism” into B(H), while the cited definition makes B(H) all bounded operators and the Remarks explicitly avoid asserting that all of them have adjoints without choice. Step 2.1 correctly constructs adjoints for the represented image. Clarify that star-preservation refers to these image adjoints, or name the adjointable-operator subalgebra as target.

alerts.finding: Published supplier lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction, Proof 1.2, says the map (u,v)↦⟨u,u₀⟩⟨v,v₀⟩ “is $\mathbb C$-linear on $H\times K$”. It is bilinear, not linear on the product vector space: with H=K=C and u₀=v₀=1, its values at (1,1) and 2(1,1) are 1 and 4, rather than 1 and 2. The intended descent uses the induced additive map on the free presentation and the balanced bilinear relations; the quoted linearity assertion itself is incorrect.

seams_checked.note: Read the supplier page and its Clifford definition, polarization, universal-property and PBW items against the consuming proofs. The consumer uses the same plus-Q quotient, complex symmetric bilinear form, characteristic-not-two hypothesis and finite ordered basis. PBW is applied in dimension 2n to obtain 2^(2n), including n=0. No ungraded Clifford/exterior isomorphism is inferred.

Read the supplier page and its actual matrix-C*-algebra item. The CAR proof uses that item only for M_m(C) with m=2^n≥1, its operator norm, conjugate-transpose involution and completeness. It does not import the page's AC-dependent general GNS results into the choice-free occupation branch.
